title: Tailored SLO Transition Toolkit for Enterprise Clients
author: Lena Park
body:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook is a product-focused toolkit for enterprise customers who are migrating inference workloads between Redwood deployment modes (hosted -> Dedicated or hosted -> Private). It defines a repeatable process to translate customer-facing SLOs into platform controls, consumption profiles, and pricing guardrails. The goal is to ensure predictable latency, cost, and availability during and after migration while minimizing production impact.

Audience
- Product managers and solution architects leading migrations
- Customer success and solutions engineering
- Platform and runtime engineers responsible for capacity and rollout

Scope
- Migration modalities covered: Hosted -> Dedicated, Hosted -> Private (VPC/on-prem).
- SLO types addressed: p50/p95 latency, per-request fidelity, availability (monthly uptime), error budget burn, and cost-per-1k-tokens.
- Not in scope: model retraining, dataset migrations, or legal/compliance contract changes (handled by other teams).

Goals and Success Criteria
- Clear mapping from customer SLOs to Redwood controls (routing policies, capacity reservations, fallback rules).
- Migration playbooks with <2% regression in p95 latency for 90% of customers within 48 hours of switchover.
- Cost-estimation accuracy <= 12% vs. measured 30-day post-migration consumption for standard conversational workloads.

Key Concepts
- SLO translation: converting an abstract SLA (e.g., \"95% requests under 150ms\") into technical knobs (instance size, batching targets, KV cache policy, model variant).
- Fidelity envelope: an agreed set of model/quantization variants allowed for a tenant during capacity constraints.
- Consumption contract: a committed capacity profile (reserved-GPU-hours, warm-pools) tied to billing and graceful degradation behavior.

SLO Translation Matrix (example)
This table provides an example mapping of customer SLOs to Redwood controls and the verification signals we use.

| Customer SLO | Redwood Controls | Verification Signals | Notes |
|-------------|------------------|----------------------|-------|
| p95 latency <= 200ms | Dedicated pool with 2:1 reservation; small-batch target 16 tokens; KV cache TTL 2h | p95 request latency, queueing ratio, batch sizes | Start with 1.5x headroom for first 48h |
| Availability 99.9% | SLA-backed route with dual-region fallback | error rate, failover latency, health checks | Enable automatic region failover for critical routes |
| Cost target: < $0.75 / 1k tokens | Route to quantized variant for non-critical paths; enable adaptive batching | per-token cost, sample quality evals | Quality gate required for quantized variant before enabling |

Migration phases
1) Intake & assessment (owner: solutions engineering)
   - Gather production traffic profile (sequence-length distribution, tokens per request, concurrency, peak shapes).
   - Obtain target SLOs and cost constraints from the customer.
   - Baseline measurements from hosted: 14-day traces + synthetic QPS ramp.

2) Design & capacity plan (owner: product + platform)
   - Run capacity simulation using the customer profile; recommend pool sizes, autoscaling thresholds, and warm-pool budgets.
   - Compute cost-sim and produce 3 consumption options: conservative, balanced, and aggressive.
   - Select fallback model variants and define fidelity envelope.

3) Preflight validation (owner: platform + runtime)
   - Create a staging tenant in Dedicated/Private and run 48-hour shadow traffic replay.
   - Verify SLOs: p50/p95 latency, correct batching behavior, and KV cache hit rate.

4) Canary rollout (owner: solutions engineering + SRE)
   - Gradually shift 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% traffic over KPI gates (latency, error rate, cost).
   - Monitor for anomalies for 24 hours after each step, revert on defined thresholds.

5) Post-migration stabilization (owner: customer success + platform)
   - 30-day monitoring window with weekly reconciliations and cost tuning.
   - Transition to normal support and budgeting cadence.

Pre-migration checklist (minimum required)
- [ ] Production traffic histogram (7-day, 30-day) uploaded to migration ticket
- [ ] Customer SLOs and target cost constraints documented and agreed
- [ ] Model variant compatibility matrix finalized (quantized/float16/float32)
- [ ] Security & network prerequisites validated (VPC peering, firewall rules)
- [ ] Key rotation and KMS access for Private deployments verified
- [ ] Billing & contract addendum approved if reserved capacity is required

Canary gating thresholds (example)
- Latency: p95 increase <= 10% vs hosted baseline per canary step
- Errors: request error rate increase <= 0.1% absolute
- Cost: projected effective $/1k tokens not exceed agreed consumption option by >20%
- Quality: evaluation prompts pass fidelity gate (acceptance threshold configurable, default: 95% similarity by rubric)

Rollback and fallback policies
1) Immediate fallback to hosted route if any gate is violated during canary.
2) If fallback unavailable (e.g., network failure in customer VPC), engage emergency route: model variant in Dedicated pool + reduced concurrency (throttled to safe QPS).
3) Post-rollback root-cause analysis within 48 hours following the incident retros.

Telemetry and verification
- Required telemetry signals to collect during migration: per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), batch size distribution, KV cache hit ratio, model variant usage, error type breakdown, per-route cost metrics.
- Alerting: temporary migration policy alerts for \"SLO drift\" (p95 latency > threshold), \"cost-exceed\" (consumption-run-rate > expected by 25%), and \"quality-regression\" (eval similarity below gate).
- Reconciliation cadence: daily for first 7 days, weekly for next 3 weeks.

Pricing and packaging implications
- Consumption options (decision knobs):
  - Reserved capacity (monthly commitment): lowest unit cost, requires 30-day lead time for provisioning.
  - Warm-pool subscription (short-term buffer): medium unit cost, flexible up/down monthly.
  - On-demand bursts: highest unit cost, used for occasional traffic spikes.
- Addenda: migrations that require Dedicated pools should include a migration fee to cover pre-provisioning and runbook engineering (typically 10–15% of first-month reserved cost).
- Billing reconciliation: for first billing cycle post-migration, provide a line-item report comparing projected vs actual consumption with suggested tuning actions.

Sample pricing decision table
| Consumption option | Best for | Expected unit cost delta vs hosted | Recommended contract term |
|--------------------|----------|------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| Reserved capacity | Predictable, 24/7 traffic | -20% | 12 months |
| Warm-pool subscription | Variable daytime workloads | -8% | 1–3 months |
| On-demand bursts | Spiky, unpredictable | +30% | none |

Ownership & stakeholder matrix
- Migration lead: Solutions Engineering (primary contact)
- Platform provisioning: Eng Platform
- Runtime tuning and model compatibility: Serving Runtime team
- SLO verification and SRE gating: Eng SRE
- Billing adjustments and contract changes: Finance & Legal

Risk register and mitigations (top risks)
- Unexpected p95 regressions: Mitigation: conservative headroom and quick rollback policy.
- Quality regressions with quantized variants: Mitigation: gated local evals + sample A/B tests before canary.
- Billing disputes due to consumption variance: Mitigation: pre-migration cost-sim, post-migration line-item reconciliation, and credits as required per contract.

Roadmap & milestones for the toolkit (product view)
- Q2 2027: Publish toolkit, add migration-automations to Console (guided wizard).
- Q3 2027: Telemetry templates in Console (preflight upload + trend analytics).
- Q4 2027: Automated cost-simulator in Console with contract-ready export.
- Q1 2028: Policy-driven canary automation (gates + auto-fallback) for standard enterprise bundles.

Release notes (initial release v1.0)
- v1.0 (2027-04-11): Initial publish of Tailored SLO Transition Toolkit. Includes translation matrix templates, migration playbook, canary gating thresholds, and pricing decision guidance.
- v1.1 (2027-06-20): Added warm-pool pricing guidance, updated canary thresholds based on first 10 migrations, and published evaluation rubric for quantized variants.

Appendix: Example console snippet (policy JSON as example)
Note: the snippet below is an illustrative example that operators can paste into the Console policies UI.

POLICY: DedicatedRoutePolicyExample
- route: tenant-abc-dedicated
- reservation: 2 x a100-40g
- autoscale_min: 2
- autoscale_max: 8
- batching_target_tokens: 16
- kv_cache_ttl_seconds: 7200
- fallback_route: hosted-tenant-abc
- canary_steps: [1,5,20,100]

Acceptance checklist before closure
- [ ] 30-day post-migration cost report delivered to customer
- [ ] No unresolved SLO violations older than 7 days
- [ ] Runbook updates merged and Console guided-wizard entry created
- [ ] Account moved to standard billing cadence
